title: Lateral Thinking
intro: These puzzles reward a sideways look. If the obvious answer does not fit, try a different angle.

teasers.question: A cafe sign says Free coffee tomorrow. You visit every day but never get one. Why?
teasers.hint: Think about what day it is whenever you walk in.
teasers.answer: When you arrive it is always today.
teasers.explanation: Tomorrow never arrives while you are standing there, because every visit happens on a day that is today.

teasers.question: Nobody in the quiet reading room says a word, yet two people have a long, detailed conversation there. How?
teasers.hint: Speaking is only one way to talk.
teasers.answer: They write notes or use sign language
teasers.explanation: A conversation needs two people sharing ideas, not voices. Writing, signing or typing all count.

teasers.question: A painter finishes a whole house in an afternoon without leaving her chair or touching a wall. How?
teasers.hint: Does the house have to be a real one?
teasers.answer: She paints a picture of a house.
teasers.explanation: She is an artist working on a canvas, so the house is a painting rather than a building.

teasers.question: A shelf holds 12 jars. All but 5 of them are empty. How many jars have something in them?
teasers.hint: Read the phrase all but 5 slowly.
teasers.explanation: All but 5 are empty means that 5 are not empty, so 5 jars have something in them.

teasers.question: In winter a woman crosses a wide river on foot with no bridge, boat or ford, and her shoes stay dry. How?
teasers.hint: Think about what water can turn into.
teasers.explanation: In a hard freeze the surface of a river becomes ice thick enough to walk on.

teasers.question: A train leaves at nine in the morning and arrives at nine in the morning after a long trip. It ran exactly on time. How?
teasers.hint: Clocks do not show the same time everywhere.
teasers.answer: It travelled into a time zone that is behind, or it arrived the next day.
teasers.explanation: Clocks change from one time zone to another, so a trip can take hours and still end at the same clock time. Arriving a day later works too.
